question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both sides of the equation by $4+6\text{i}$ to isolate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-5\text{i} & =(p+\text{i}q)(4+6\text{i}) \\ \frac{1-5\text{i}}{4+6\text{i}} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to simplify the fraction on the left-hand side, we multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(1-5\text{i})(4-6\text{i})}{(4+6\text{i})(4-6\text{i})} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{4-6\text{i}-20\text{i}+30{\text{i}}^{2}}{{4}^{2}-(6\text{i})^{2}} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{-26-26\text{i}}{16+36} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{-26-26\text{i}}{52} & =p+\text{i}q \\ -\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\text{i} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get $-\frac{1}{2}=p.$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get $-\frac{1}{2}=q.$

Therefore, $p=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $q=-\frac{1}{2}.$
